claim: X-ray histotomography is a high-resolution, non-destructive form of X-ray microtomography (micro-CT) imaging customized for three-dimensional (3D), digital histology.
source: We previously described X-ray histotomography, a high-resolution, non-destructive form of X-ray microtomography (micro-CT) imaging customized for three-dimensional (3D), digital histology, allowing quantitative, volumetric tissue and organismal phenotyping (Ding et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ding et al., 2019, which is a reference to prior work.

claim: X-ray histotomography allows quantitative, volumetric tissue and organismal phenotyping.
source: We previously described X-ray histotomography, a high-resolution, non-destructive form of X-ray microtomography (micro-CT) imaging customized for three-dimensional (3D), digital histology, allowing quantitative, volumetric tissue and organismal phenotyping (Ding et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ding et al., 2019.

claim: Ionic silver staining combined with micro-CT can characterize melanin distribution in whole zebrafish larvae.
source: Here, we have combined micro-CT with a novel application of ionic silver staining to characterize melanin distribution in whole zebrafish larvae.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the manuscript, demonstrated through experimental data and imaging.

claim: Normalized micro-CT reconstructions of silver-stained fish consistently reproduced pigment patterns seen by light microscopy.
source: Normalized micro-CT reconstructions of silver-stained fish consistently reproduced pigment patterns seen by light microscopy, and further allowed direct quantitative comparisons of melanin content across wild-type and mutant samples, including subtle phenotypes not previously noticed.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing light microscopy and micro-CT images, as shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Silver staining micro-CT allowed direct quantitative comparisons of melanin content across wild-type and mutant samples.
source: Normalized micro-CT reconstructions of silver-stained fish consistently reproduced pigment patterns seen by light microscopy, and further allowed direct quantitative comparisons of melanin content across wild-type and mutant samples, including subtle phenotypes not previously noticed.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data presented in Tables 1, 3, 4 and Figures 3 and 5.

claim: Silver staining micro-CT revealed subtle phenotypes not previously noticed.
source: Normalized micro-CT reconstructions of silver-stained fish consistently reproduced pigment patterns seen by light microscopy, and further allowed direct quantitative comparisons of melanin content across wild-type and mutant samples, including subtle phenotypes not previously noticed.
evidence: This is supported by the observation of decreased melanin content in mitfaw2/w2 RPE, which was not previously reported.

claim: Silver staining of melanin for micro-CT provides proof-of-principle for whole-body, 3D computational phenomic analysis of a specific cell type at cellular resolution.
source: Silver staining of melanin for micro-CT provides proof-of-principle for whole-body, 3D computational phenomic analysis of a specific cell type at cellular resolution, with potential applications in other model organisms and melanocytic neoplasms.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The zebrafish is an important vertebrate model organism for developmental biology, functional genomics, and large-scale drug and toxicological screens.
source: The zebrafish (Danio rerio) is an important vertebrate model organism for developmental biology, functional genomics, and large-scale drug and toxicological screens due to its high fecundity, transparent, externally developing embryos, relatively low husbandry costs, and small size (Lieschke and Currie, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lieschke and Currie, 2007, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: Zebrafish have high fecundity, transparent externally developing embryos, relatively low husbandry costs, and small size.
source: The zebrafish (Danio rerio) is an important vertebrate model organism for developmental biology, functional genomics, and large-scale drug and toxicological screens due to its high fecundity, transparent, externally developing embryos, relatively low husbandry costs, and small size (Lieschke and Currie, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lieschke and Currie, 2007, representing established knowledge.

claim: Wild-type adult zebrafish have alternating dark and light longitudinal stripes.
source: One of the most readily observable phenotypes in the zebrafish is its distinctive pigmentation patterning, which, in wild-type adults, appears as alternating dark and light longitudinal stripes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about zebrafish pigmentation.

claim: Zebrafish stripes contain brown-black melanophores, silvery iridophores, and yellow xanthophores.
source: The study of the cellular components of these stripes, including brown-black melanophores, silvery iridophores, and yellow xanthophores, has taught us a lot about the necessary cells, genes, and pathways required for normal pigmentation development and the evolution of complex color patterning (D'Agati et al., 2017; Frohnhöfer et al., 2013; Hultman and Johnson, 2010; Kelsh, 2004; Kelsh et al., 1996; Lister, 2002; Lister et al., 1999; Singh and Nüsslein-Volhard, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations representing established knowledge.

claim: The crystal strain is a compound mutant with defects in both melanogenesis and iridophore development that never develops pigment.
source: For example, the crystal (mitfaw2/w2; mpv17a9/a9; slc45a2b4/b4) strain, a compound mutant with defects in both melanogenesis and iridophore development, never develops pigment and is used for applications where transparent post-embryonic organisms are required, such as fluorescence imaging (Antinucci and Hindges, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Antinucci and Hindges, 2016.

claim: The golden mutant (slc24a5b1/b1) produces an early, dramatic reduction in eye and body melanin content.
source: Another pigmentation mutant, golden (slc24a5b1/b1), is frequently used for mutagenesis screening or testing of gene editing technology because its single affected locus produces an early, dramatic reduction in eye and body melanin content that has been implicated in human skin color (Doyon et al., 2008; Ginger et al., 2008; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Lamason et al., 2005; Moore et al., 2006; Streisinger et al., 1981; Streisinger et al., 1989).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The golden mutation has been implicated in human skin color.
source: Another pigmentation mutant, golden (slc24a5b1/b1), is frequently used for mutagenesis screening or testing of gene editing technology because its single affected locus produces an early, dramatic reduction in eye and body melanin content that has been implicated in human skin color (Doyon et al., 2008; Ginger et al., 2008; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Lamason et al., 2005; Moore et al., 2006; Streisinger et al., 1981; Streisinger et al., 1989).
evidence: This is supported by citations, particularly Lamason et al., 2005.

claim: Melanin is a heterogeneous mix of cross-linked derivatives of the amino acid tyrosine.
source: Melanin, the dark pigment produced in zebrafish melanophores, is a heterogeneous mix of cross-linked derivatives of the amino acid tyrosine.
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge about melanin.

claim: In humans, melanin is produced in skin melanocytes and transferred to keratinocytes which prevents UV-based DNA damage.
source: In humans, melanin is produced in skin melanocytes and transferred to keratinocytes which prevents UV-based DNA damage; this pigment is the major component of human skin and hair color with implications in human health and disease (Slominski et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Slominski et al., 2004, representing established knowledge.

claim: Melanin is the major component of human skin and hair color with implications in human health and disease.
source: In humans, melanin is produced in skin melanocytes and transferred to keratinocytes which prevents UV-based DNA damage; this pigment is the major component of human skin and hair color with implications in human health and disease (Slominski et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Slominski et al., 2004.

claim: Dysfunction of human pigmentation is responsible for diseases such as albinism and vitiligo.
source: Dysfunction of human pigmentation is responsible for diseases such as albinism and vitiligo.
evidence: This is established medical knowledge.

claim: Overgrowth of melanocytes can result in melanocytic nevi or malignant melanoma with darkly pigmented lesions.
source: Overgrowth of melanocytes can result in melanocytic nevi or malignant melanoma with darkly pigmented lesions.
evidence: This is established medical knowledge.

claim: Neuromelanin is produced as a byproduct of dopamine synthesis and stains the substantia nigra pars compacta in the basal ganglia.
source: In addition, neuromelanin, produced as a byproduct of dopamine synthesis, stains the substantia nigra pars compacta in the basal ganglia, the region principally lost in Parkinson's disease (Kumar et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kumar et al., 2015.

claim: The substantia nigra pars compacta is the region principally lost in Parkinson's disease.
source: In addition, neuromelanin, produced as a byproduct of dopamine synthesis, stains the substantia nigra pars compacta in the basal ganglia, the region principally lost in Parkinson's disease (Kumar et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kumar et al., 2015, representing established medical knowledge.

claim: Assessments of pigmentation patterns and cell morphology in zebrafish have been largely descriptive due to challenges of melanin quantification at cellular resolution in whole animals.
source: Despite the importance of melanin patterning and distribution for developmental and functional studies, assessments of pigmentation patterns and cell morphology have been largely descriptive due to the challenges of melanin quantification at cellular resolution, particularly in whole animals.
evidence: This is an inference based on the state of the field and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Zebrafish pigmentation studies have generally relied on light microscopy and two-dimensional photography for phenotyping.
source: In zebrafish, pigmentation studies have generally relied on light microscopy and two-dimensional photography for phenotyping, with pigmentation interpreted as counts of pigmented/unpigmented cells in a particular region of the fish in a manner that is, at best, semi-quantitative (D'Agati et al., 2017; Frohnhöfer et al., 2013; Hultman and Johnson, 2010; Kelsh, 2004; Kelsh et al., 1996; Lister, 2002; Lister et al., 1999; Moore et al., 2006; Singh and Nüsslein-Volhard, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work in the field.

claim: Fluorescence techniques may readily tag melanophores, but fluorescence is quenched or blocked by melanin itself.
source: Fluorescence techniques may readily tag melanophores, but fluorescence is quenched or blocked by the melanin itself and such techniques are limited in penetration due to the light-scattering properties of soft tissues (Antinucci and Hindges, 2016; Hultman and Johnson, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Antinucci and Hindges, 2016 and Hultman and Johnson, 2010.

claim: Fluorescence techniques are limited in penetration due to the light-scattering properties of soft tissues.
source: Fluorescence techniques may readily tag melanophores, but fluorescence is quenched or blocked by the melanin itself and such techniques are limited in penetration due to the light-scattering properties of soft tissues (Antinucci and Hindges, 2016; Hultman and Johnson, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations and represents established knowledge about fluorescence microscopy limitations.

claim: Electron microscopy techniques provide only a small field of view of pigment cells and lack 3D context.
source: Electron microscopy techniques, while exquisitely detailed, provide only a small field of view (FOV) of pigment cells and lack 3D context (Hirata et al., 2003; Hirata et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hirata et al., 2003 and 2005, and represents known limitations of electron microscopy.

claim: Photoacoustic/optoacoustic microscopy has been used to produce 3D pigmentation patterns in whole zebrafish larvae over time.
source: Photoacoustic/optoacoustic microscopy has been used to produce 3D pigmentation patterns in whole zebrafish larvae over time, but while such images can have high lateral resolution, they are limited in axial resolution by the ultrasound wavelength (Kneipp et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kneipp et al., 2015.

claim: Photoacoustic/optoacoustic microscopy images are limited in axial resolution by the ultrasound wavelength.
source: Photoacoustic/optoacoustic microscopy has been used to produce 3D pigmentation patterns in whole zebrafish larvae over time, but while such images can have high lateral resolution, they are limited in axial resolution by the ultrasound wavelength (Kneipp et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kneipp et al., 2015.

claim: MRI and PET imaging techniques that take advantage of melanin's metal scavenging or binding properties do not provide the spatial resolution needed for detailed studies of pigment patterns.
source: Other imaging techniques have taken advantage of melanin's unique metal scavenging or binding properties, such as MRI or PET imaging, but these techniques do not provide the spatial resolution needed for detailed studies of pigment patterns (Cheng et al., 2011; Enochs et al., 1997; Ren et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cheng et al., 2011, Enochs et al., 1997, and Ren et al., 2009.

claim: X-ray microtomography (micro-CT) is a 3D imaging technique that uses a series of X-ray projections to reconstruct small samples at high, isotropic resolution without the need for sectioning.
source: X-ray microtomography (micro-CT) is a 3D imaging technique that uses a series of X-ray projections to reconstruct small samples at high, isotropic resolution without the need for sectioning.
evidence: This is established knowledge about micro-CT technology.

claim: Micro-CT optimized for cellular feature detection in whole zebrafish samples (histotomography) with soft tissue contrast enhancement through staining with phosphotungstic acid was previously reported.
source: We previously reported an implementation of micro-CT optimized for cellular feature detection in whole zebrafish samples (histotomography) with soft tissue contrast enhancement through staining with phosphotungstic acid (Ding et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ding et al., 2019, referring to prior work by the authors.

claim: Reconstructed X-ray attenuation values are proportional to the amount of stained material in a sample.
source: Because reconstructed X-ray attenuation values are proportional to the amount of stained material in a sample, micro-CT images have been used for quantitative studies of development and gene expression, even in optically opaque samples (Metscher and Müller, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Metscher and Müller, 2011, and represents a fundamental principle of micro-CT imaging.

claim: The silver staining procedure is based on the reduction of silver used for histological Fontana-Masson staining.
source: The procedure, based on the reduction of silver used for histological Fontana-Masson staining (Bancroft, 2008), appears highly specific to melanin and preserves native pigment distribution in whole specimens.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Bancroft, 2008, describing the histological method.

claim: The silver staining procedure appears highly specific to melanin and preserves native pigment distribution in whole specimens.
source: The procedure, based on the reduction of silver used for histological Fontana-Masson staining (Bancroft, 2008), appears highly specific to melanin and preserves native pigment distribution in whole specimens.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing melanin-specific staining in the manuscript.

claim: Wild-type zebrafish and mutant strains including golden and body pigment-deficient mutants (nacre/casper) were imaged for visualization and quantitative analyses of zebrafish melanin.
source: To demonstrate the utility of this technique, we imaged wild-type zebrafish as well as mutant strains with unique pigmentation patterns, including golden and body pigment-deficient mutants (nacre/casper) (D'Agati et al., 2017; Lister et al., 1999; White et al., 2008), for visualization and quantitative analyses of zebrafish melanin.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and images presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Zebrafish were housed in a recirculating system at an average temperature of 28°C on a 14 hr:10 hr light:dark cycle.
source: Zebrafish were housed in a recirculating system at an average temperature of 28°C on a 14 hr:10 hr light:dark cycle.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used.

claim: Embryos and larvae were raised in darkness and staged according to a standard developmental staging series.
source: Embryos and larvae were raised in darkness and staged according to a standard developmental staging series (Kimmel et al., 1995).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods, with citation to Kimmel et al., 1995 for the staging series.

claim: 5 days post-fertilization (dpf) larvae were euthanized in pre-chilled Tricaine-S solution buffered with 1% PBS for at least 60 s.
source: Briefly, 5 days post-fertilization (dpf) larvae were euthanized in pre-chilled Tricaine-S (MS-222, 200 mg/L) solution (Syndel USA, Ferndale, WA) buffered with 1% phosphate buffered saline (PBS) for at least 60 s and fixed overnight (>20 hr) in chilled 10% neutral buffered formalin (Fisher Scientific, Allentown, PA) in a flat-bottom glass container at room temperature with gentle agitation.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used.

claim: Fixed specimens were fixed overnight in chilled 10% neutral buffered formalin.
source: Briefly, 5 days post-fertilization (dpf) larvae were euthanized in pre-chilled Tricaine-S (MS-222, 200 mg/L) solution (Syndel USA, Ferndale, WA) buffered with 1% phosphate buffered saline (PBS) for at least 60 s and fixed overnight (>20 hr) in chilled 10% neutral buffered formalin (Fisher Scientific, Allentown, PA) in a flat-bottom glass container at room temperature with gentle agitation.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used.

claim: Ammoniacal silver solution was produced by adding concentrated ammonium hydroxide solution dropwise to a 2.5% silver nitrate solution until the resulting tan-brown precipitate dissolved.
source: Prior to staining, ammoniacal silver solution was produced in a chemical fume hood by adding concentrated ammonium hydroxide solution dropwise to a 2.5% silver nitrate solution until the resulting tan-brown precipitate dissolved, then left undisturbed overnight until the solution stayed clear.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used.

claim: Individual larvae were stained for 18 hr in ammoniacal silver solution in flat-bottom glass containers with gentle agitation at room temperature.
source: Individual larvae were washed three times for 5 min each in ddH2O and then stained for 18 hr in ammoniacal silver solution in flat-bottom glass containers with gentle agitation at room temperature.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used.

claim: Pilot experiments indicated that gold toning step did not increase X-ray contrast and it was eliminated in subsequent procedures.
source: Although the histological Fontana-Masson staining procedure typically includes a gold toning step (whereby a gold chloride wash replaces silver with gold), pilot experiments indicated that this step did not increase X-ray contrast and it was thus eliminated in subsequent procedures (data not shown).
evidence: This is based on pilot experimental data mentioned but not shown.

claim: Micro-CT imaging was performed on Beamline 8.3.2 at the Advanced Light Source at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.
source: Micro-CT imaging was performed on Beamline 8.3.2, Tomography (micro-CT), at the Advanced Light Source (ALS) at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL, Berkeley, CA).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used.

claim: An X-ray energy of 26 keV was used to optimize silver-based contrast.
source: A double-multilayer monochromator was used to select an X-ray energy of 26 keV to optimize silver-based contrast (elemental silver K edge = 25.5 keV) (Hubbell and Seltzer, 2004).
evidence: This is based on the known K edge of silver, cited to Hubbell and Seltzer, 2004.

claim: Elemental silver K edge is 25.5 keV.
source: A double-multilayer monochromator was used to select an X-ray energy of 26 keV to optimize silver-based contrast (elemental silver K edge = 25.5 keV) (Hubbell and Seltzer, 2004).
evidence: This is a physical constant cited to Hubbell and Seltzer, 2004.

claim: Whole 5 dpf larval zebrafish were imaged over two scans, covering head and tail regions, respectively.
source: Whole 5 dpf larval zebrafish were imaged over two scans, covering head and tail regions, respectively.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used.

claim: Each constant motion scan resulted in 1017 projections over 180° with an exposure time of 175 ms per projection.
source: Each constant motion scan resulted in 1017 projections over 180° with an exposure time of 175 ms per projection.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used.

claim: Flat field correction, ring artifact reduction, and image reconstruction were performed using the open source TomoPy toolkit.
source: Flat field correction, ring artifact reduction, and image reconstruction were performed using the open source TomoPy toolkit (Gürsoy et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a description of the computational methods used, with citation to the software.

claim: Images were reconstructed using Gridrec with ring artifact reduction and a second-order Butterworth filter with a cutoff of 0.2 to reduce noise.
source: Images were reconstructed using Gridrec (Dowd et al., 1999; Rivers, 2012) with ring artifact reduction (Miqueles et al., 2014; Münch et al., 2009) and a second-order Butterworth filter with a cutoff of 0.2 to reduce noise, resulting in a nominal isotropic voxel size of 0.52 µm, as estimated by the number of reconstructed voxels spanning the 1.03 mm outer diameter of the reconstructed polyimide sample tube.
evidence: This is a description of the computational methods used, with citations to the algorithms.

claim: The nominal isotropic voxel size was 0.52 µm.
source: Images were reconstructed using Gridrec (Dowd et al., 1999; Rivers, 2012) with ring artifact reduction (Miqueles et al., 2014; Münch et al., 2009) and a second-order Butterworth filter with a cutoff of 0.2 to reduce noise, resulting in a nominal isotropic voxel size of 0.52 µm, as estimated by the number of reconstructed voxels spanning the 1.03 mm outer diameter of the reconstructed polyimide sample tube.
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data.

claim: Reconstructions were normalized to the LR White resin present in every sample to allow direct comparisons between scans.
source: This 'cleaned up' data was normalized to the LR White resin present in every sample to allow direct comparisons between scans as follows: An average attenuation coefficient for the resin in each reconstruction (µresin) was determined as the mean intensity value over all slices of a 100-pixel × 100-pixel square of empty resin, distant from the sample or sides of the tube.
evidence: This is a description of the data processing methods used.

claim: 3D rendering and analysis, including registration of head and tail segments, were performed using Avizo versions 2020.1 and 2020.2.
source: 3D rendering and analysis, including registration of head and tail segments, were performed using Avizo versions 2020.1 and 2020.2 (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
evidence: This is a description of the computational methods used.

claim: A combination of thresholding and manual segmentation was used to assign voxels in merged datasets to established larval pigmented regions.
source: A combination of thresholding and manual segmentation was used to assign voxels in merged datasets to established larval pigmented regions, including left and right retinal pigment epithelia (RPE), dorsal stripe, ventral stripe, yolk sac stripe, and left and right lateral stripes.
evidence: This is a description of the data analysis methods used.

claim: An unstained wild-type zebrafish exhibited negligible X-ray attenuation and no pigment pattern upon reconstruction.
source: Under the same conditions, an unstained wild-type zebrafish exhibited negligible X-ray attenuation and no pigment pattern upon reconstruction (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: A single slice from a representative reconstruction of a 5 dpf wild-type larva shows high intensity regions of stained sample (RPE and body pigment), the resin embedding medium, and the inner and outer walls of the polyimide tubing.
source: A single slice from a representative reconstruction of a 5 dpf wild-type larva that was rotated and cropped to the region of interest is presented in Figure 1B. Several key features of the reconstruction have been highlighted, including the high intensity regions of stained sample (RPE and body pigment), the resin embedding medium, and the inner and outer walls of the polyimide tubing used for embedding.
evidence: This is supported by the image in Figure 1B.

claim: The reconstructed isotropic voxel resolution was estimated at 0.52 µm.
source: By dividing the number of voxels spanning the polyimide tube by its outer diameter (1.03 mm), we estimated our reconstructed isotropic voxel resolution at 0.52 µm; isotropic resolution enabled rotation and re-slicing of the volume without distortion.
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data.

claim: Isotropic resolution enabled rotation and re-slicing of the volume without distortion.
source: By dividing the number of voxels spanning the polyimide tube by its outer diameter (1.03 mm), we estimated our reconstructed isotropic voxel resolution at 0.52 µm; isotropic resolution enabled rotation and re-slicing of the volume without distortion.
evidence: This is a known property of isotropic imaging.

claim: Microscopic air bubbles formed in all samples at the tube-resin interface due to resin shrinkage during polymerization.
source: We also noted that microscopic air bubbles formed in all samples at the tube-resin interface, sometimes close to the zebrafish sample, due to resin shrinkage during polymerization.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: All the surface melanin features evident in the light micrograph were also observed in the micro-CT image.
source: The top of the head represents a unique 'fingerprint' pattern for each larva, and all the surface melanin features evident in the light micrograph were also observed in the micro-CT image.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of light microscopy and micro-CT images in Figure 1D.

claim: Pigment units lying deep in the fish that are obscured by soft tissue in light microscopy were readily discernable in micro-CT reconstructions.
source: Pigment units lying deep in the fish that are obscured by soft tissue in light microscopy were readily discernable in micro-CT reconstructions, demonstrating the sensitivity of this new assay.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of light microscopy and micro-CT images in Figure 1D.

claim: The wild-type larval zebrafish forms a stereotypical ontogenetic pigmentation pattern with four longitudinal 'stripes' of melanin by approximately 3 dpf: dorsal, lateral, ventral, and yolk sac.
source: The wild-type larval zebrafish forms a stereotypical ontogenetic pigmentation pattern with pigment cell precursors starting from the neural crest at the dorsum and spreading ventrally, eventually forming four longitudinal 'stripes' of melanin by approximately 3 dpf: dorsal, lateral, ventral (above the air bladder), and yolk sac (below the yolk) (Kelsh, 2004; Kelsh et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kelsh, 2004 and Kelsh et al., 1996, representing established knowledge.

claim: The majority of the larval pigment pattern has matured by 5 dpf.
source: After this pattern is formed from direct-developing melanophores, pigment stem cells fill in gaps in the patterns or are responsible for pigment cell regeneration such that the majority of the larval pigment pattern has matured by 5 dpf (Hultman and Johnson, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hultman and Johnson, 2010.

claim: In 3D, the dorsal, ventral, and yolk sac stripes were observed as flattened sheets of pigment cells that often met in the midline of the fish and followed the curves of body structures.
source: In 3D, we observed the dorsal, ventral, and yolk sac stripes as flattened sheets of pigment cells that often met in the midline of the fish and followed the curves of body structures (Figure 2B–C, Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by 3D renderings shown in Figure 2B-C and Video 1.

claim: The two lateral stripes were made up of intermittent thin, flat accumulations of melanin, one stripe on each side of the larva.
source: In contrast, the two lateral stripes were made up of intermittent thin, flat accumulations of melanin, one stripe on each side of the larva (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: This is supported by 3D renderings shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: Larval zebrafish raised on white backgrounds aggregate melanin within melanophores while those raised on black backgrounds disperse melanin throughout the melanophores.
source: Zebrafish can adapt their pigmentation to their environment for camouflage; larval zebrafish raised on white backgrounds aggregate melanin within melanophores while those raised on black backgrounds disperse melanin throughout the melanophores (Logan et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Logan et al., 2006.

claim: Larvae reared in a closed, dark incubator exhibited a dispersed staining phenotype on micro-CT with sheets of pigment and indistinct cell boundaries.
source: Our larvae, reared in a closed, dark incubator, exhibited a dispersed staining phenotype on micro-CT with sheets of pigment and indistinct cell boundaries.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: The dorsal, ventral, and yolk sac stripes exhibited ovoid transparencies in the melanin staining that are approximately 9.29 µm in length (SD = ±1.23 µm).
source: Notably, the dorsal, ventral, and yolk sac stripes exhibited ovoid transparencies in the melanin staining that are approximately 9.29 µm in length (SD = ±1.23 µm, Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, and Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by measurements shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The transparencies in melanin staining represent large organelles, likely nuclei, which are devoid of melanin.
source: We suspect that these transparencies represent large organelles, likely nuclei, which are devoid of melanin.
evidence: This is an inference based on the size and appearance of the transparencies, supported by comparison to prior work.

claim: This observation is consistent with high-resolution photographs of black background-adapted dorsal melanophores reported previously.
source: This observation is consistent with high-resolution photographs of black background-adapted dorsal melanophores reported previously (Logan et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Logan et al., 2006.

claim: Zebrafish melanophores have been frequently shown to be multinucleated.
source: Several of these transparencies were in close proximity (Figure 2D); zebrafish melanophores have been frequently shown to be multinucleated (Usui et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Usui et al., 2018.

claim: Pigment units not associated with the four larval stripes tended to have a globular, condensed morphology.
source: In contrast to the flattened, diffuse melanin in the stripes, pigment units not associated with the four larval stripes tended to have a globular, condensed morphology.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: Cells deeper in the soft tissue of the fish were individually separated and dendritic, particularly in the anterior portion of the head.
source: These cells, deeper in the soft tissue of the fish, were individually separated and dendritic, particularly in the anterior portion of the head (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by the image in Figure 2E.

claim: The RPE is one of the outermost layers of the retina, contacting the choroidal vasculature on its outer surface and the outer nuclear layer of the retina on its inner surface.
source: The RPE is one of the outermost layers of the retina, contacting the choroidal vasculature on its outer surface and the outer nuclear layer of the retina on its inner surface.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge.

claim: The RPE is a critical structure for vertebrate visual function.
source: It is a critical structure for vertebrate visual function.
evidence: This is established knowledge about RPE function.

claim: Unlike the neural crest-derived body melanophores, the RPE develops from the optic neuroepithelium and is closely associated with the photoreceptor cells of the developing retina.
source: Unlike the neural crest-derived body melanophores, the RPE develops from the optic neuroepithelium and is closely associated with the photoreceptor cells of the developing retina (Antinucci and Hindges, 2016; Bharti et al., 2006; Gestri et al., 2012; Schmitt and Dowling, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations representing established knowledge.

claim: The outer surface of the RPE was relatively smooth and contiguous, except for a ridge where the choroidal fissure fused during development.
source: The outer surface was relatively smooth and contiguous, except for a ridge where the choroidal fissure fused during development.
evidence: This is an observation from the 3D renderings shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The inner surface of the RPE exhibited regular villous protrusions toward the center of the eye where the apical side of the RPE cells invaginate into the inner nuclear layer.
source: The inner surface exhibited regular villous protrusions toward the center of the eye where the apical side of the RPE cells invaginate into the inner nuclear layer.
evidence: This is an observation from the 3D renderings shown in Figure 2F.

claim: A hole in the ventromedial portion of the RPE indicated the location of the optic nerve egress.
source: A hole in the ventromedial portion of the RPE indicated the location of the optic nerve egress.
evidence: This is an observation from the 3D renderings shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Despite not having melanin, the dense, fibrous lens stained weakly with silver and its center was partially visible in the reconstructions.
source: Interestingly, despite not having melanin, the dense, fibrous lens stained weakly with silver and its center was partially visible in our reconstructions, providing consistent anatomical landmarks across all samples.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: Micro-CT reconstructions are inherently quantitative, with information at each voxel about the local concentration of stained material.
source: One of the advantages of micro-CT reconstructions is that they are inherently quantitative, with information at each voxel about the local concentration of stained material.
evidence: This is a known property of micro-CT imaging.

claim: The normalized intensity values were assumed proportional to the local density of silver deposition, and therefore melanin concentration, throughout each sample.
source: The resulting normalized intensity values, although arbitrary units, were assumed proportional to the local density of silver deposition, and therefore melanin concentration, throughout each sample and could be compared directly between individual stained fish.
evidence: This is an assumption underlying the quantitative analysis.

claim: Total melanin-containing volume covered 4.87 × 10^6 µm^3 (SD = ±3.78 × 10^5 µm^3) of the average 5 dpf wild-type larva.
source: Total melanin-containing volume covered 4.87 × 106 µm3 (SD = ±3.78 × 105 µm3) of the average 5 dpf wild-type larva, much of which was distributed between the two eyes.
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data shown in Table 1.

claim: Standard deviation of the segmented regions, as percentage of the average melanin volumes between siblings, was on par with individual volume variation between brain regions of 5 dpf zebrafish (±11.9%) reported previously.
source: The melanin-containing volumes of symmetrical structures (the RPE and lateral stripes) for each fish were similar, and standard deviation of the segmented regions, as percentage of the average melanin volumes between siblings, was on par with individual volume variation between brain regions of 5 dpf zebrafish (±11.9%) reported previously (Ding et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior work cited to Ding et al., 2019.

claim: 62.8% (SD = ±1.1%) of the melanin in the average 5 dpf wild-type larva was contained in the RPE.
source: In Figure 3B we report the melanin content of the wild-type larvae as percentages of total melanin; 62.8% (SD = ±1.1%) of the melanin in the average 5 dpf wild-type larva was contained in the RPE.
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Table 1.

claim: Approximately 1.1% (SD = ±0.05%) of stained material was not associated with the eyes or four main stripes, mostly in the nose.
source: Approximately 1.1% (SD = ±0.05%) of stained material was not associated with the eyes or four main stripes, mostly in the nose (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data.

claim: Distribution of melanin was highly concordant between the three scanned wild-type larvae.
source: Distribution of melanin was highly concordant between the three scanned larvae.
evidence: This is an observation from the quantitative data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The golden zebrafish line is a prototypical model of human skin color, with a mutation in the potassium-dependent sodium/calcium exchanger gene slc24a5.
source: The golden zebrafish line is a prototypical model of human skin color, with a mutation in the potassium-dependent sodium/calcium exchanger gene slc24a5 (slc24a5b1/b1).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the golden mutant.

claim: A mutation in the human homolog of slc24a5, SLC24A5, is a major contributor to the skin color differences between people of African and European ancestry.
source: A mutation in the human homolog of this gene, SLC24A5, is a major contributor to the skin color differences between people of African and European ancestry.
evidence: This is established knowledge, likely from Lamason et al., 2005.

claim: The slc24a5b1/b1 zebrafish line has a delay in larval pigmentation and a dramatic reduction in larval and adult melanin content throughout the body and eyes.
source: The slc24a5b1/b1 zebrafish line has a delay in larval pigmentation and a dramatic reduction in larval and adult melanin content throughout the body and eyes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the golden mutant phenotype.

claim: At the electron microscope level, golden melanophores contain fewer melanosomes that are less densely pigmented and irregularly shaped.
source: At the electron microscope level, golden melanophores contain fewer melanosomes that are less densely pigmented and irregularly shaped (Lamason et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lamason et al., 2005.

claim: The most striking characteristic of the silver-stained slc24a5b1/b1 larvae was a globally diminished intensity corresponding to the decreased melanin content in these mutants.
source: As opposed to wild-type reconstructions, which exhibited intense whole-body staining on micro-CT imaging (Figure 4A), the most striking characteristic of the silver-stained slc24a5b1/b1 larvae was a globally diminished intensity corresponding to the decreased melanin content in these mutants (Figure 4D, Video 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Video 2.

claim: While wild-type pigment reconstructions formed essentially contiguous sheets down the length of the larval body, melanin staining in the golden mutant was discontinuous and fragmented throughout.
source: In addition, while wild-type pigment reconstructions formed essentially contiguous sheets down the length of the larval body (Figure 4A–B), melanin staining in the golden mutant was discontinuous and fragmented throughout (Figure 4D–E).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Although melanin was diminished throughout the body, the dorsal, lateral, ventral, and yolk sac stripes, as well as other melanin deposits in the nose and eyes, were all identified in the golden mutant in an organization similar to the pigmentation in wild-type larvae.
source: Although melanin was diminished throughout the body, the dorsal, lateral, ventral, and yolk sac stripes, as well as other melanin deposits in the nose and eyes, were all identified in the golden mutant in an organization similar to the pigmentation in wild-type larvae (Figure 4E, Video 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 4E and Video 2.

claim: In addition to less intense staining, the golden fish had thinner stained areas in the RPE.
source: Single slices of the micro-CT reconstructions through the middle of the eyes of wild-type (Figure 4C) and golden (Figure 4F) larvae indicated that in addition to less intense staining, the golden fish had thinner stained areas in the RPE.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 4C and 4F.

claim: The mitfaw2/w2 mutation results in the nacre zebrafish line, which lacks all body melanin but retains the optic neuroepithelium-derived RPE melanophores.
source: The mitfaw2/w2 mutation results in the nacre zebrafish line, which lacks all body melanin but retains the optic neuroepithelium-derived RPE melanophores (Lister et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lister et al., 1999.

claim: An additional mutation in iridophore development gene mpv17 (mpv17a9/a9) produces the compound mutant line casper, notable for its transparent adult body useful for fluorescence imaging.
source: An additional mutation in iridophore development gene mpv17 (mpv17a9/a9) produces the compound mutant line casper, notable for its transparent adult body useful for fluorescence imaging (D'Agati et al., 2017; White et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to D'Agati et al., 2017 and White et al., 2008.

claim: Larvae with the mitfaw2/w2 mutant background exhibited staining almost entirely in the RPE in micro-CT scans.
source: As expected, larvae with the mitfaw2/w2 mutant background exhibited staining almost entirely in the RPE in our micro-CT scans, and as such we only used the head segment for visualization and analysis (Figure 4G, Video 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 4G and Video 2.

claim: Staining intensity, size, and shape of the eyes in mitfaw2/w2 larvae were similar to those of wild-type larvae.
source: Staining intensity, size, and shape of the eyes were similar to those of wild-type larvae, but body-stripe pigment or melanin deposits in the nose were completely absent.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: Body-stripe pigment or melanin deposits in the nose were completely absent in mitfaw2/w2 larvae.
source: Staining intensity, size, and shape of the eyes were similar to those of wild-type larvae, but body-stripe pigment or melanin deposits in the nose were completely absent.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: A rendering of segmented volumes confirmed the absence of the dorsal, lateral, ventral, and yolk sac stripes in mitfaw2/w2 larvae, and also highlighted disorganized argentaffin material posterior to the eyes.
source: A rendering of these segmented volumes (Figure 4H, Video 2) confirmed the absence of the dorsal, lateral, ventral, and yolk sac stripes, and also highlighted disorganized argentaffin material posterior to the eyes.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 4H and Video 2.

claim: Argentaffin material was also present in the wild-type and golden samples but was generally overshadowed by the intensely staining melanin.
source: Such material was also present in the wild-type and golden samples (included in the 'other' staining category), but was generally overshadowed by the intensely staining melanin.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: Single micro-CT slices through the eyes of the mitfaw2/w2 mutant revealed an RPE layer of similar thickness and intensity to the wild type.
source: Single micro-CT slices through the eyes of the mitfaw2/w2 mutant revealed an RPE layer of similar thickness and intensity to the wild type (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: For each pigment region, a statistically significant difference between the groups was found using a series of one-way ANOVAs.
source: For each pigment region, a statistically significant difference between the groups was found using a series of one-way ANOVAs (Table 2).
evidence: This is a result of statistical analysis of the experimental data shown in Table 2.

claim: The slc24a5b1/b1 larvae exhibited a 75.3% decrease in mean segmented melanin volume from wild-type.
source: Overall, the slc24a5b1/b1 larvae exhibited a 75.3% decrease in mean segmented melanin volume (p = 0.000005) from wild-type while the mitfaw2/w2 fish exhibited a 63.1% decrease (p = 0.000015, Figure 5A).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data shown in Figure 5A and Table 3.

claim: The mitfaw2/w2 fish exhibited a 63.1% decrease in mean segmented melanin volume from wild-type.
source: Overall, the slc24a5b1/b1 larvae exhibited a 75.3% decrease in mean segmented melanin volume (p = 0.000005) from wild-type while the mitfaw2/w2 fish exhibited a 63.1% decrease (p = 0.000015, Figure 5A).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data shown in Figure 5A and Table 4.

claim: Total melanin content showed an 83.8% decrease in slc24a5b1/b1 larvae from wild-type.
source: Total melanin content (the cumulative sum of intensity in the segmented regions) followed a similar trend with an 83.8% decrease in slc24a5b1/b1 larvae (p = 0.000004) and a 55.0% decrease in mitfaw2/w2 larvae (p = 0.000040, Figure 5B).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Table 3.

claim: Total melanin content showed a 55.0% decrease in mitfaw2/w2 larvae from wild-type.
source: Total melanin content (the cumulative sum of intensity in the segmented regions) followed a similar trend with an 83.8% decrease in slc24a5b1/b1 larvae (p = 0.000004) and a 55.0% decrease in mitfaw2/w2 larvae (p = 0.000040, Figure 5B).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Table 4.

claim: The slc24a5b1/b1 RPE exhibited a 65.4% decrease in melanin volume from wild-type RPE.
source: The slc24a5b1/b1 RPE exhibited a 65.4% decrease in melanin volume (p = 0.001) and an 80.5% decrease in melanin content from wild-type RPE (p = 0.000058).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data shown in Figure 5C-D and Table 3.

claim: The slc24a5b1/b1 RPE exhibited an 80.5% decrease in melanin content from wild-type RPE.
source: The slc24a5b1/b1 RPE exhibited a 65.4% decrease in melanin volume (p = 0.001) and an 80.5% decrease in melanin content from wild-type RPE (p = 0.000058).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data shown in Figure 5C-D and Table 3.

claim: The mitfaw2/w2 mutant exhibited a 28.5% decrease in melanin content from the wild-type RPE.
source: Although the mitfaw2/w2 mutant is generally considered to have normal eye pigmentation, we found that it exhibited a 28.5% decrease in melanin content from the wild-type RPE (p = 0.014), potentially linked to an observed 25.1% decrease in RPE volume, which was not statistically significant (p = 0.06).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data shown in Figure 5C-D and Table 4.

claim: The mitfaw2/w2 mutant exhibited an observed 25.1% decrease in RPE volume, which was not statistically significant.
source: Although the mitfaw2/w2 mutant is generally considered to have normal eye pigmentation, we found that it exhibited a 28.5% decrease in melanin content from the wild-type RPE (p = 0.014), potentially linked to an observed 25.1% decrease in RPE volume, which was not statistically significant (p = 0.06).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data shown in Figure 5C-D and Table 4.

claim: RPE melanin made up 99.9% (SD = ± 0.02%) of the observed staining in the mitfaw2/w2 larvae.
source: Interestingly, because RPE melanin made up 99.9% (SD = ± 0.02%) of the observed staining in the mitfaw2/w2 larvae, this smaller decrease in eye melanin content still left the mitfaw2/w2 fish with more total melanin than the golden fish, which had consistently and dramatically diminished melanin throughout the body and eyes (Figure 5B, D, F).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data.

claim: The smaller decrease in eye melanin content in mitfaw2/w2 still left these fish with more total melanin than the golden fish.
source: Interestingly, because RPE melanin made up 99.9% (SD = ± 0.02%) of the observed staining in the mitfaw2/w2 larvae, this smaller decrease in eye melanin content still left the mitfaw2/w2 fish with more total melanin than the golden fish, which had consistently and dramatically diminished melanin throughout the body and eyes (Figure 5B, D, F).
evidence: This is an inference from the quantitative data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Silver staining for melanin micro-CT has applications for other model organisms, as well as human biopsies for diseases like melanoma.
source: Silver staining for melanin micro-CT has applications for other model organisms, as well as human biopsies for diseases like melanoma, and represents a model for the 3D quantitative analysis of specific biological features using micro-CT.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications.

claim: The silver staining technique described appears to be highly specific for melanin.
source: The silver staining technique described here appears to be highly specific for melanin.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data showing melanin-specific staining.

claim: Micro-CT provides high-resolution 3D images which are inherently digital reconstructions of the scanned sample, directly enabling quantification of signal intensity (melanin content).
source: Micro-CT provides high-resolution 3D images which are inherently digital reconstructions of the scanned sample, directly enabling quantification of signal intensity (melanin content).
evidence: This is a known property of micro-CT imaging demonstrated in this study.

claim: A wide FOV and 3D registration of multiple scans allowed investigation of the entire volumes of 5 dpf wild-type and mutant larvae.
source: A wide FOV and 3D registration of multiple scans allowed us to investigate the entire volumes of our 5 dpf wild-type and mutant larvae.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach used.

claim: Preliminary experiments have indicated that the technique is equally applicable to larger samples.
source: Preliminary experiments have indicated that the technique is equally applicable to larger samples, which are more difficult to investigate with light-based microscopy techniques but are readily accessible using micro-CT.
evidence: This is based on preliminary experimental data not shown in detail.

claim: Micro-CT imaging involves fixation and staining of samples and exposure to high flux X-rays.
source: Micro-CT imaging involves fixation and staining of samples and exposure to high flux X-rays.
evidence: This is a known characteristic of the micro-CT technique.

claim: Future studies of melanin at different stages of development or during experimental time courses using this method will require multiple samples of different ages with enough individuals of each stage to account for normal variation in zebrafish pigmentation.
source: Therefore, future studies of melanin at different stages of development or during experimental time courses using this method will require multiple samples of different ages with enough individuals of each stage to account for normal variation in zebrafish pigmentation.
evidence: This is an inference about future experimental design based on the limitations of the technique.

claim: Silver deposition was assumed to be stoichiometric with the local concentration of melanin such that the arbitrary units of reconstructed intensity were proportional to the amount of stained material in the original sample.
source: For our measurements, we assumed that silver deposition was stoichiometric with the local concentration of melanin such that the arbitrary units of reconstructed intensity were proportional to the amount of stained material in the original sample.
evidence: This is an assumption underlying the quantitative analysis.

claim: By performing staining under the same conditions and for the same amount of time for all samples, and normalizing reconstructions to a common background material, samples could be compared directly.
source: By performing our staining under the same conditions and for the same amount of time for all of our samples, and normalizing our reconstructions to a common background material, we were able to compare our samples directly.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach used to enable quantitative comparisons.

claim: Silver staining and micro-CT imaging may more thoroughly describe zebrafish mutants that have already been identified with effects on larval, juvenile, and adult pigmentation.
source: Silver staining and micro-CT imaging may more thoroughly describe zebrafish mutants that have already been identified with effects on larval, juvenile, and adult pigmentation (Parichy, 2006), and our work with the nacre/casper zebrafish highlights the potential to identify new mutants with subtler effects on pigment localization or concentration.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications, with citation to Parichy, 2006.

claim: Work with the nacre/casper zebrafish highlights the potential to identify new mutants with subtler effects on pigment localization or concentration.
source: Silver staining and micro-CT imaging may more thoroughly describe zebrafish mutants that have already been identified with effects on larval, juvenile, and adult pigmentation (Parichy, 2006), and our work with the nacre/casper zebrafish highlights the potential to identify new mutants with subtler effects on pigment localization or concentration.
evidence: This is supported by the finding of decreased melanin content in mitfaw2/w2 RPE.

claim: High-resolution, whole-animal 3D images of melanin could help experimentally confirm computational models of pigment cell interactions or studies of human skin color.
source: Zebrafish are frequently used for studying complex animal pigmentation patterning, including computational models of pigment cell interactions (Owen et al., 2020) or studies of human skin color (Lamason et al., 2005). High-resolution, whole-animal 3D images of melanin could help experimentally confirm such studies.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications, with citations to Owen et al., 2020 and Lamason et al., 2005.

claim: Darkly pigmented lesions in transgenic or transplanted zebrafish can be tracked and scored to investigate the genetic underpinnings of melanoma origin and spread.
source: Darkly pigmented lesions in transgenic or transplanted zebrafish can be tracked and scored to investigate the genetic underpinnings of melanoma origin and spread (Ceol et al., 2011; Fazio et al., 2021); silver staining and micro-CT imaging could enable computational phenotyping and direct detailed morphological analysis of lesions in their native context.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ceol et al., 2011 and Fazio et al., 2021.

claim: Silver staining and micro-CT imaging could enable computational phenotyping and direct detailed morphological analysis of melanoma lesions in their native context.
source: Darkly pigmented lesions in transgenic or transplanted zebrafish can be tracked and scored to investigate the genetic underpinnings of melanoma origin and spread (Ceol et al., 2011; Fazio et al., 2021); silver staining and micro-CT imaging could enable computational phenotyping and direct detailed morphological analysis of lesions in their native context.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications.

claim: Human mm- to cm-scale melanocytic nevi or melanoma biopsy samples may be stained for micro-CT imaging to enable quantitative morphological analyses of these samples.
source: Human mm- to cm-scale melanocytic nevi or melanoma biopsy samples may be stained for micro-CT imaging as described in this study to enable quantitative morphological analyses of these samples.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications.

claim: Silver staining may be combined with other histotomography stains, such as phosphotungstic acid, to provide tissue context for melanin localization.
source: Silver staining may also be combined with other histotomography stains, such as phosphotungstic acid, to provide tissue context for melanin localization.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications.

claim: Dual-energy CT may be used to deconvolute multi-stained samples into component elemental materials.
source: Dual-energy CT may be used to deconvolute such multi-stained samples into component elemental materials (Liu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications, with citation to Liu et al., 2009.

claim: Silver-based staining has been used previously for micro-CT imaging using antibody-mediated deposition for molecular targets in chick embryos.
source: Notably, silver-based staining has been used previously for micro-CT imaging using antibody-mediated deposition for molecular targets in chick embryos (Metscher and Müller, 2011); our work suggests that melanin-mediated silver deposition may confound such a strategy in pigmented samples.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Metscher and Müller, 2011.

claim: Melanin-mediated silver deposition may confound antibody-mediated silver staining strategies in pigmented samples.
source: Notably, silver-based staining has been used previously for micro-CT imaging using antibody-mediated deposition for molecular targets in chick embryos (Metscher and Müller, 2011); our work suggests that melanin-mediated silver deposition may confound such a strategy in pigmented samples.
evidence: This is an inference based on the findings of this study.

claim: Silver staining of melanin opens the possibility of targeted melanin deposition for micro-CT molecular imaging using the prophenoloxidase reporter system in Drosophila.
source: However, silver staining of melanin also opens the possibility of targeted melanin deposition for micro-CT molecular imaging using, for example, the prophenoloxidase reporter system in Drosophila (True et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications, with citation to True et al., 2001.

claim: The raw micro-CT reconstructions described in this study were on the order of 80–100 GB per scan.
source: The raw micro-CT reconstructions described in this study were on the order of 80–100 GB per scan, which can be challenging to work with for users with only standard computing resources or without familiarity with 3D image analysis.
evidence: This is a description of the data generated in this study.

claim: An online, open-source ViewTool was expanded to include a browser-based volumetric viewer based on the open-source Three.js project.
source: To make our 3D pigmentation renderings more generally accessible without requiring the user to download full volumes, we have expanded our online, open-source ViewTool (http://3D.fish) (Ding et al., 2019) to include a browser-based volumetric viewer (http://3D.fish/stains/silver) based on the open-source Three.js project (https://threejs.org).
evidence: This is a description of a resource created as part of this study, with citation to Ding et al., 2019.

claim: The volumetric viewer contains all of the wild-type and mutant samples described in this study, with customizable visualization options and toggles for viewing the segmented pigment region labels.
source: This volumetric viewer contains all of the wild-type and mutant samples described in this study, with customizable visualization options and toggles for viewing the segmented pigment region labels.
evidence: This is a description of a resource created as part of this study.
